mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q01.stem: A nut driver is used to tighten a compatible hex nut by turning the nut side.
reasons: Also called a box driver, it must fit the nut’s across-flats dimension and available workspace.
This statement is true. Also called a box driver, it must fit the nut’s across-flats dimension and available workspace.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q02.stem: Play when reversing a feed mechanism is called the machined surface’s roughness.
reasons: This statement is false. Reversal play is backlash; surface roughness is the fine unevenness of a machined surface.
Reversal play is backlash; surface roughness is the fine unevenness of a machined surface.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q03.stem: For a screw advancing 0.5 mm per turn and a thimble divided into 50, one division is 0.1 mm.
reasons: This statement is false. 0.5 mm÷50=0.01 mm; 0.1 mm is ten times too large.
0.5 mm÷50=0.01 mm; 0.1 mm is ten times too large.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q04.stem: An aluminum electrolytic capacitor uses an aluminum-oxide film as its dielectric.
reasons: It is an example of conductors separated by dielectric; check polarity and ratings for each type.
This statement is true. It is an example of conductors separated by dielectric; check polarity and ratings for each type.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q05.stem: Reducing counts by changing counting rules alone proves real improvement.
reasons: This statement is false. Do not confuse changed aggregation conditions with improvement.
Do not confuse changed aggregation conditions with improvement.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q06.stem: Any part that looks like resin always remains safely insulating regardless of damage or temperature.
reasons: This statement is false. A material name alone does not guarantee suitability.
A material name alone does not guarantee suitability.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q07.stem: Using resistance ratios for voltage division assumes a series connection carrying the same current.
reasons: Check voltage-divider applicability conditions.
This statement is true. Check voltage-divider applicability conditions.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q08.stem: NOT passes its input through unchanged.
reasons: This statement is false. Negation inverts the input.
Negation inverts the input.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q09.stem: hFE is a universal constant for every load, temperature and current.
reasons: This statement is false. Characteristics vary with conditions.
Characteristics vary with conditions.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q10.stem: Even flexible boards require checks of bending positions, cycle counts and other conditions.
reasons: Flexibility does not mean unlimited permission.
This statement is true. Flexibility does not mean unlimited permission.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q11.stem: The voltage ratio of an ideal transformer always depends only on the difference between its two turn counts.
reasons: This statement is false. Use V2/V1=N2/N1.
Use V2/V1=N2/N1.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q12.stem: Observing reversed motion alone does not establish a particular valve failure.
reasons: Classifying symptoms differs from establishing the cause.
This statement is true. Classifying symptoms differs from establishing the cause.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q13.stem: Check management condition for torque tools requiring calibration and pre-use checks.
reasons: Tool integrity and the specified range matter.
This statement is true. Tool integrity and the specified range matter.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q14.stem: Pilot holes must equal the nominal thread diameter exactly for every material.
reasons: This statement is false. Distinguish pilot diameter from nominal diameter.
Distinguish pilot diameter from nominal diameter.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q15.stem: Practical multiple-choice questions may test judgment and planning as well as knowledge.
reasons: Check the method and question format described in the materials.
This statement is true. Check the method and question format described in the materials.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q16.stem: Stay clear of suspended loads and follow designated handling methods.
reasons: Consider dropping and unexpected movement of the load.
This statement is true. Consider dropping and unexpected movement of the load.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q17.stem: Design quality means actual manufactured characteristics, while manufacturing quality means only the design’s intended characteristics.
reasons: This statement is false. Design quality concerns intended characteristics; manufacturing quality concerns achieved workmanship. Do not reverse them.
Design quality concerns intended characteristics; manufacturing quality concerns achieved workmanship. Do not reverse them.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q18.stem: Aligned points for two variables eliminate any need to consider other factors.
reasons: This statement is false. Distinguish correlation from causation.
Distinguish correlation from causation.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q19.stem: Specific gravity is a ratio to a reference density and has no unit.
reasons: Distinguish density from a density ratio.
This statement is true. Distinguish density from a density ratio.
This statement is false. 210×297 mm is A4.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q21.stem: The main purpose of laminating a core from thin sheets is to increase losses caused by flux changes.
reasons: This statement is false. Thin laminations and similar measures reduce losses caused by changing flux.
Thin laminations and similar measures reduce losses caused by changing flux.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q22.stem: The passive-component classification does not imply absence of residual charge or heating.
reasons: It also includes components storing and releasing energy.
This statement is true. It also includes components storing and releasing energy.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q23.stem: At a node, total current flowing in must equal total current flowing out.
reasons: Check the current balance.
This statement is true. Check the current balance.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q24.stem: Connecting a measuring instrument never affects the circuit or measured value.
reasons: This statement is false. Consider the measurement system’s influence.
Consider the measurement system’s influence.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q25.stem: Some SSR products require checking off-state leakage, heat and other conditions.
reasons: Functional off and safe isolation differ.
This statement is true. Functional off and safe isolation differ.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q26.stem: Environmental testing and a one-off functional check examine different conditions.
reasons: Evidence under the specified environment is needed.
This statement is true. Evidence under the specified environment is needed.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q27.stem: Part release is unrelated to mold design, so draft angles need not be checked.
reasons: This statement is false. Ease of removal is also controlled through mold design.
Ease of removal is also controlled through mold design.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q28.stem: Voltage-waveform rise and timing differences between signals may be observed.
reasons: These concern signal changes over time.
This statement is true. These concern signal changes over time.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q29.stem: Every FRP type has an entirely scratch-proof surface and no disposal requirements.
reasons: This statement is false. Consider constraints as well as benefits.
Consider constraints as well as benefits.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q30.stem: A chemical container may display several hazards.
reasons: Check multiple items of hazard information.
This statement is true. Check multiple items of hazard information.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-practical-q01.stem: In a sine-wave circuit containing only an ideal inductor, what is current’s phase relative to voltage?
reasons: Sine-wave voltage and current have a defined phase.
Ideal inductors produce lag; lead confuses them with ideal capacitors.
Ideal-inductor current lags voltage. Real circuits also involve resistance and other effects.
An ideal inductor alone produces a phase difference rather than equal phase.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-practical-q02.stem: Why does output continue after releasing the start button in a basic holding circuit?
options: An output-related contact creates a path retaining the start condition.
Inputs and outputs have no relationship.
Every relay remains energized forever without power.
Only because the stop button is disabled.
reasons: A contact maintains the state after operation. Trace separately whether stop conditions release it.
The input, contacts and coil form the holding relationship.
Ordinary electromagnetic relays do not remain energized forever without power.
Self-holding does not mean disabling stop; stop conditions must release it.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-practical-q03.stem: 12 mA enters a node and divides into 4 mA and an unknown branch. What is the unknown current?
reasons: Input and output totals match:12=4+I, so I=8 mA.
The ratio12/4 does not calculate the unknown branch current.
Adding outgoing4 to incoming12 violates node conservation.
The product12×4 is not a current-sum conservation equation.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-practical-q04.stem: Glass-fiber and carbon-fiber boards look equally black and are mixed together. What should you do?
options: Assume all FRP is perfectly insulating.
Ignore material records if the shape fits.
Assume all properties match because colors match.
Compare material and required properties; do not substitute by appearance.
reasons: FRP containing carbon fiber cannot universally be called perfectly insulating.
Shape compatibility does not replace checking material identity and specifications.
Identical black appearance does not establish matching fiber and resin properties.
Fiber and resin affect electrical and mechanical properties. Shape and appearance alone cannot guarantee conformity.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-practical-q05.stem: For binary x=1 and y=0, what is NOT(x+y)?
reasons: Binary values are zero or one, not two.
OR gives one, but the outer NOT changes it to zero.
x+y is OR, yielding one; negating gives zero. De Morgan’s NOT x AND NOT y also gives zero.
The result depends on inputs, so the function is not constantly one.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-practical-q06.stem: A basic off-delay output is on when its input turns off. With a four-second setting, when does the output turn off?
options: It stays on forever regardless of input.
reasons: Basic off-delay switches off after the set time from input-off. Check product power and holding conditions.
The setting is four seconds, not permanent holding.
Basic off-delay retains output for the set time rather than switching off immediately.
Timing starts at input-off, not before input-on.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-practical-q07.stem: A scatter plot suggests a relationship between temperature and defect rate. Which conclusion is justified?
options: Declare temperature the cause without verification.
Treat it as a candidate relationship and investigate other factors and conditions.
Delete all points to remove correlation.
reasons: Correlation alone does not prove temperature causes defects.
Correlation does not establish causation. Check conditions and other factors to verify causes.
Deleting points loses measured facts and prevents checking the relationship.
Specification changes do not verify causes and cannot be made without authorization.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-practical-q08.stem: After soldering, solder connects to the neighboring pad. What condition is this?
reasons: A solder connection may eliminate required insulation spacing.
Unwanted conductive bridging is not a normal tolerance assessment.
Flux presence differs from a metallic bridge to an adjacent pad.
An unwanted bridge joins neighboring areas. Use approved rework and reinspection.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-practical-q09.stem: A designated terminal shelf has a lower limit of 10 and upper limit of 30, but contains7. Which report follows the three fixed rules?
options: Call the 23-unit gap from the maximum a defect count.
Report that the specified item is three below the lower limit.
The shelf location means the stock is appropriate.
Add other parts to make up the number.
reasons: The gap from 30 is not a defect count; the relevant shortage is three below the lower limit.
The rules control location, item and quantity. Seven is three below ten; mixing other items does not fix it.
Correct location alone does not meet the quantity condition.
Other items do not resolve the required item’s shortage and may cause wrong use.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-practical-q10.stem: A full-scale100 scale reads40 with a50 mA range selected. What is the measurement?
reasons: 40 is the scale indication before converting to the selected 50 mA range.
50 mA is full scale, not the 40/100 pointer position.
40/100×50 mA=20 mA. Do not use the scale number alone.
